standard_prerequisites.name: The short exact sequence associated to a quasi-compact open immersion
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma giving the short exact sequence 0 -> j_!G -> j_*G -> i_*i^{-1}j_*G -> 0 for the inclusion of the complement with its reduced structure
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the exact sequence expressing the extension by zero as a kernel.

standard_prerequisites.name: Commutation with products of the pushforwards and of the pullback along a closed immersion
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma that the pullback along a closed immersion commutes with products
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the commutation with products of i^{-1}, while j_* and i_* commute with products as right adjoints.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness of products in the category of sheaves on the pro-etale site
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cohomology on Sites, the proposition on enough weakly contractibles, which implies that products are exact in the category of abelian sheaves
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the exactness of products, which passes the commutation with products from the other terms of the sequence to j_!.

core_obligations: Reduce to products (proof lines 5411-5414): since j_! is exact it suffices to prove that it commutes with products, and the question is local on X, so one may assume X affine.

Write j_! as a kernel (proof lines 5414-5420): for an abelian sheaf G on U one has j^{-1}j_*G = G, so the exact sequence of the open immersion gives 0 -> j_!G -> j_*G -> i_*i^{-1}j_*G -> 0, where i is the inclusion of the reduced complement.

Compare the commutation with products (proof lines 5420-5426): the pushforwards j_* and i_* commute with products because they are right adjoints, and i^{-1} commutes with products by the cited lemma for closed immersions; since products are exact on the pro-etale site, the kernel j_! inherits the commutation with products, which gives the statement for limits because j_! is exact.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the commutation with products and to an affine base.
Express the extension by zero as the kernel of a map between functors that visibly commute with products.
Use exactness of products to conclude for the kernel.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a quasi-compact open immersion j : U -> X the extension by zero on the pro-etale sites commutes with limits (statement lines 5401-5407). The proof (proof lines 5409-5428) reduces to the commutation with products and to an affine base, expresses the extension by zero as the kernel of a map between functors commuting with products, and concludes by the exactness of products on the pro-etale site. H2: a three-step reduction with three inputs, written out in full.
